clue.text: Just like poet with regular rap: Number One after Number One

indicators.note: after means the first number one, ME, is placed following the second, I

parts.note: in the nick means in prison, which is where a regular rap (a repeated criminal charge) puts you
oft is the poetic form of often, a word a poet would use
I is the first person, number one
me, oneself, is number one

explanation.surface: Someone praises a poet's steady rhythm, then muses on chart-toppers following one another.
explanation.walkthrough: The two 'Number One' phrases give different words: the first is ME, placed after the second, I, to finish the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving at the last possible moment is arriving 'just' in time, the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Ravel works on Fantasia? Don't think so

indicators.note: to ravel is to tangle, so the letters are tangled into a new order; it also poses as the composer

explanation.surface: A sceptic doubts that the composer Ravel had any hand in the Disney film Fantasia.
explanation.walkthrough: Ravel the French composer is the misdirection; as a verb it tangles the letters of WORKS ON FANTASIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a hedged denial, a polite way of expressing doubt about a claim.

clue.text: Universities welcome first of girls attending a two-part induction

parts.note: hi is a greeting of welcome

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of girls

parts.note: here, present, means attending

indicators.note: two-part tells us to split the word induction into its two parts, IN and DUCTION, so it reads as an instruction to put the a in the rest

parts.note: the letters left once the leading IN is read as an instruction

explanation.surface: Universities greet incoming female students at a two-part induction session.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is to read 'a two-part induction' as 'a IN DUCTION': A goes inside DUCTION to give DUCATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Universities provide tertiary schooling, collectively called the higher stage of learning.

clue.text: Strip suspended by guys at High School Prom?

definitions.text: Strip suspended by guys at High School Prom?

parts.words: Strip suspended by guys at High School Prom?
parts.note: a strip of cloth hung from the necks of boys dressed up for an American school dance

explanation.surface: It sounds like a striptease act being banned by the boys at a school dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip' and 'suspended' suggest a ban on undressing; really the strip is fabric hanging from the young men. A prom is an American school formal dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is a narrow band of cloth worn hanging from the collar, standard dress for a formal dance.

clue.text: Spell in Glasgow is fully protected from slashers?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a Scots word for a magic spell or trick
second meaning, read as two words

explanation.surface: Someone in Glasgow is safe from knife attackers for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: Glasgow flags a Scottish word; the second half is a whimsical reading of the word split as CAN'T RIP.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish dialect the word names a charm or piece of witchcraft, a magic incantation.

clue.text: Compose smashing love song for performance at the Minack?

indicators.note: smashing in the sense of crashing together, so love and compose are joined

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, the letter O
to pen is to compose, as in writing music or verse
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A composer is told to write a terrific love song for a staging at the Minack.
explanation.walkthrough: The Minack is a famous theatre carved into a Cornish clifftop with no roof.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minack has no roof, so its shows are staged outdoors, under the sky.

clue.text: "Mains Supply Free!" — article promoted London residence

indicators.note: promoted means moved up to the top, the front of a down answer

parts.note: supply read as an adverb, supplely, bends the letters of mains into a new order
on the house means free of charge
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A slogan promises free mains electricity or water, as though from a utility advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' poses as a noun; read as 'supplely' it rearranges MAINS to MANSI. Then THE, the article inside ON THE HOUSE, is lifted to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mansion House is the official home of the Lord Mayor of the City of London.

clue.text: Factory yards off limits further satisfy POTUS

parts.note: a mill is a factory

indicators.note: the limits, the outer letters, of yards are taken off

parts.note: to fill an order is to satisfy it
more means further, additionally

explanation.surface: A complaint that factory yards being closed off serves only to please the President.
explanation.walkthrough: POTUS stands for President of the United States; this is the thirteenth one.
explanation.definitionFit: Millard Fillmore served as the thirteenth American President, from 1850 to 1853.

clue.text: Special label for men only

parts.note: a tag is a label

explanation.surface: A special label marks something as restricted to men.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag party or stag night is an event attended exclusively by males.

clue.text: Scullery-maid recalled sketchily in parts

indicators.note: something recalled sketchily is remembered in a jumbled way, so the letters are muddled
parts means splits up and spreads out, so the letters of in are mixed through the rest

explanation.surface: Someone only half remembers a kitchen servant in a few scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale heroine toils among the cinders as a kitchen servant before the ball.

clue.text: The key one's left 12 inches away

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I'S

indicators.note: away means the foot is taken out of the word left

parts.note: twelve inches make a foot, abbreviated FT

explanation.surface: Something important has been left a foot away.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' looks like a reference to 12-across, but it is just twelve inches, a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A key, or cay, is a low island, as in the Florida Keys.

clue.text: A fresh am-dram act collects material on the way

indicators.note: fresh means new, so the letters are made into something new

explanation.surface: An amateur dramatics group puts on a new act and gathers material for the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmacadam is the crushed stone and tar surfacing laid on roads.

clue.text: Reh Caop's new, proper, job?

parts.note: Reh Caop is a poacher written backwards, someone turned round; the job such a reformed figure takes is to guard game

explanation.surface: It reads like a question about the new job of someone strangely named.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'poacher turned gamekeeper' describes someone who switches sides; here the word poacher is literally turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says a reformed poacher becomes the estate worker who protects game birds.

clue.text: Adoption of a single currency? It won't get off the ground

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Economic and Monetary Union, the European project to share one currency

definitions.text: It won't get off the ground
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints that a European single currency is doomed; that is just one meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation names Europe's monetary union, and the same letters name a bird that cannot fly.

clue.text: Sight of the Year

indicators.note: of means the answer is taken from within the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the and the start of Year

explanation.surface: An eye-catching spectacle is crowned the sight of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across the two words after 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is the sense, or organ, of vision, which this word also names.

clue.text: Fusses about Pop

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ados are fusses

explanation.surface: Someone makes a fuss about their father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like Dad; here it is fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Pop is a fizzy soft drink, and this word is another name for a carbonated beverage.

clue.text: Out cycling to border

indicators.note: cycling means the letters go round, the last moving to the front

parts.note: to abut is to border on

explanation.surface: Someone goes out cycling towards a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Taboo, spelt this way as a variant, means forbidden, ruled out of bounds.

clue.text: Start for Usain, individual breaking so very fast

indicators.note: breaking means splitting another word open by going inside it

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus

indicators.note: start for picks the first letter of Usain

parts.note: a person is an individual

explanation.surface: Usain Bolt, a remarkable individual, starts and breaks records at great speed.
explanation.walkthrough: SIC is the Latin 'thus', used in print to mean 'so written'.
explanation.definitionFit: Faster than the speed of sound is about as fast as speed descriptions go.

clue.text: A little edge to exotically refurbished hostelry bars

indicators.note: refurbished means done up anew, so the letters are put into a new order
bars means keeps out, so a letter is excluded from the rearranged word
the edge to exotically is its first letter

explanation.surface: An inn has been done up exotically and its bars have a fancy edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bars' looks like the pub's counters; it means excludes, so the E is left out of the letters of HOSTELRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortly means in a little while, soon, so 'in a little' gives the sense.

clue.text: Put on buffalo's skin? It can't hurt

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means the first part sits on top of the second

parts.note: to place something is to put it

indicators.note: the skin of buffalo is its outer letters

parts.note: the outer letters of buffalo

explanation.surface: Someone is told to wear a buffalo hide, with assurances it is harmless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It can't hurt' is fair because a dummy pill has no active effect, good or bad.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy pill given in trials contains no drug, so it is harmless by design.

clue.text: Hot chicken and potato — a filling roll

indicators.note: filling means going inside the other word

parts.note: a roster is a roll or list of names

explanation.surface: A menu offers hot chicken and potato in a filled bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roll' looks like bread for the sandwich; it is a list.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a scorching day, a bird fit for the oven, and a spud suited to the oven.

clue.text: Before lawyer on counter, say, a Whiskey and Coke cocktail

indicators.note: before means the cola comes ahead of the lawyer
counter means running the opposite way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a nip is a small measure of whiskey
Coke is a brand of cola
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A drinker orders a whiskey and coke at the bar before meeting their lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like a bar top; it means the A NIP is reversed. 'say' just marks a nip as an example of a whiskey.
explanation.definitionFit: The pina colada is a mixed drink of rum, pineapple and coconut.

clue.text: Women with this difficulty will be restored to health

indicators.note: W with this gives the healed word, so the answer is that word less the W

parts.note: whole once meant healthy, healed

explanation.surface: A promise that women with a certain ailment will get better.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits in the middle: W added to this difficulty makes WHOLE, restored to health.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a hole is to be in trouble, so the word names a predicament.

clue.text: A negative master plan includes choice of successor

parts.note: no is a negative answer

indicators.note: includes means the plan word holds another inside it

parts.note: intent is a plan or purpose
M is an abbreviation for master, as in MA

explanation.surface: A negative master plan is drawn up that includes choosing an heir.
explanation.definitionFit: Anointing someone, figuratively, is naming them the chosen heir to a role.

clue.text: There may be trouble ahead … water outspreading on bend

indicators.note: in an across answer, the water placed on the bend means it comes after it

parts.note: a U-bend is a bend in a pipe
the water molecule spread out shows its atoms as H, O, H

explanation.surface: A plumber notices water spreading from a bend in the pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Water is H2O; written out atom by atom it is HOH.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is said when one senses a problem coming, like the song's warning line.

clue.text: In a spin FT left Yard what we own nearly all the time

indicators.note: in means the following words go inside FT
a spin turns the letters round so they read backwards

parts.note: went means left, departed
what we own is ours
even can mean nearly or almost, as in an old usage

explanation.surface: A reporter at the Financial Times quits Scotland Yard, leaving almost all our possessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a spin' turns FT round to TF, and WENT plus Y goes inside it to make TWENTYF.
explanation.definitionFit: The numeric phrase means 24 hours a day, 7 days a week: constantly.
